title: Windows and WSL
summary: The native Windows installer uses uv-managed Python 3.12+; macOS/Linux remain 3.11+. install.ps1 bootstraps the uv version CI pins. The installer and yoke update build the Yoke tool environment from the exact Python patch uv resolves, never uv's minor-version link, so the CLI also runs over SSH. When uv reports os error 448 (Windows Redirection Guard, which OpenSSH sessions run under), install.ps1 and install.py refuse with windows_untrusted_mount_point and direct users to a local PowerShell. --wsl teaches the separate Ubuntu route. Status, path doctor and uninstall report persistent user PATH and retain uv-owned entries. Native Windows acceptance and support remain pending. The source POSIX launcher shim installer refuses on Windows and directs users to the public Windows installer. Native Windows onboarding advises installing Git for Windows on PATH and retrying from a new terminal when Git is missing. Shared platform owners handle process custody, links and file locks; POSIX uid access refuses explicitly on native Windows. Profiles use the reset-preserved identity store directly. On Linux, setup Review and doctor share one warning when the project checkout is under /mnt/<drive>; setup warns but still adopts the folder. Windows preflight treats WSL as absent when no distribution is registered under the user's Lxss registry key, even though Windows 11 ships a wsl.exe stub: it never runs wsl.exe and reports no incomplete probe. PowerShell can drop inner quotes from inline JSON passed to yoke.cmd. For declarations, browser steps and artifact metadata, save the JSON with Out-File -Encoding utf8 and pass the quoted @FILE argument. yoke.cmd exits with the command's own exit code, so PowerShell $LASTEXITCODE and cmd %ERRORLEVEL% see failures; the installer and yoke update rewrite the shim. yoke ui up starts the detached dashboard through yoke.cmd, never the extensionless sh shim beside it, and yoke ui down stops the whole cmd.exe chain; an env name with characters other than letters, digits, - and _ refuses ui_env_name_unsupported, because the name passes through cmd.exe.
